intent: One selectable option of a RadioGroup, identified by a value unique within that group.
typical_uses: One entry in a RadioGroup's set of mutually exclusive options

dont_use_when.situation: An independent yes/no control with no sibling options to choose between

invariants.text: `value` identifies this item within its nearest RadioGroup; the group selects by comparing this value against its own `value`/`defaultValue` by identity, not by which item renders first or how many precede it.

Setting `aria-invalid="true"` on an item tints its border to the destructive color; a checked item's border stays the primary checked color even while invalid - the checked state wins over the invalid one.

anti_patterns.dont: Render a RadioGroupItem outside any RadioGroup
anti_patterns.do_instead: Mount it inside a RadioGroup - the group holds the shared value, arrow-key navigation and the single-selection contract; an item outside one has no state to read or write

anti_patterns.dont: Reuse the same `value` for two items under one RadioGroup
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give every item a unique `value` within its own group - the group selects by value identity (see value-identifies-item-within-its-group), so items sharing a value show as checked together and cannot be told apart

a11y.by: Base UI's own Radio primitive (role="radio", a hidden native input for form submission, aria-checked and data-checked/data-unchecked wiring) plus radio-group.test.tsx's own role/aria-checked/data-disabled assertions

value.states: value is the item's own generic Value type parameter, required and typed by the caller
value.because: Base UI's Radio.Root declares `value: Value` with no `?` - required, and typed by the caller's own generic parameter, so no JSON Schema type can state what it holds, only that it must be present. It is compared by identity against the nearest RadioGroup's own `value`/`defaultValue`.

inputRef.states: inputRef is a ref to the hidden native input Base UI renders for form submission
inputRef.because: `React.Ref<HTMLInputElement>` is a union of a ref object and a callback function - neither is expressible in JSON Schema. It exists so a consumer can read or focus this item's own hidden input directly.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the item's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - neither expressible in JSON Schema.

style.states: style accepts a function of the item's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (checked, disabled, readOnly, required, ...). A JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through radio-group.module.css, not through this.

unexposed_parts.part: Base UI's Radio.Indicator and the kit's own fixed inner dot
unexposed_parts.reason: The kit's RadioGroupItem composes Base UI's Radio.Root around Radio.Indicator and a fixed decorative dot into one exported component; this contract describes the exported Root surface, not the internal indicator composition, so Indicator's own props are not part of it.

good.title: An item captioned by a sibling Label, inside a group
good.code:
<RadioGroup value={tier} onValueChange={setTier} aria-label="Plan tier">
  <RadioGroupItem value="pro" id="tier-pro" />
  <Label htmlFor="tier-pro">Pro</Label>
</RadioGroup>

good.title: A disabled item, named directly for assistive tech

bad.title: An item with no RadioGroup around it
bad.why: RadioGroupItem has no selection state of its own - it reads and writes the nearest RadioGroup's value through Base UI context, so mounting it outside one renders a control that never checks itself.

It exists so a consumer can read or focus this item's own hidden input directly.
